assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field of tunable moire quantum matter. It is a clear discovery with a theory that predicted the flat bands and an experiment that realized them, in a system whose structure is defined by exactly the interface and stacking control that I judge by materials standards.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observations. Yuan Cao carried out the first experiments but is not among the credited names, so a theory-plus-experiment pair is the fairest supplied configuration; Bistritzer is the junior theory co-author and is left out to keep a focused citation.
assessment.maturity: Observations have been reproduced by many independent groups over about eight years, with spectroscopy and microscopy (including scanning probe imaging of twist-angle disorder) supporting the picture. The interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Role of the first experimental author (not on the supplied list) in credit allocation.
Sample-to-sample twist-angle inhomogeneity complicates which results are intrinsic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength trapping idea and brought to extreme accuracy by Ye, are a genuine invention with lasting impact: they redefine precision metrology, test fundamental constants and open relativistic geodesy. The concept is clear, original and has been demonstrated at the 1e-18 level.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early strontium clocks; Ye's group drove the performance frontier. The two supplied names form a natural, clean pair. Other groups contributed to ion clocks and to the comb enabling technology, but those are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent laboratories worldwide and used in international comparison; a redefinition of the second is under discussion. Highly mature, and a timely complement to earlier frequency-comb recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap in AMO precision-measurement recognition already given for frequency combs and ion traps.
Allocation relative to ion-clock pioneers is outside the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the identification of three-dimensional topological insulators reshaped condensed-matter physics and surface-state spectroscopy. It combines a clear theoretical discovery with decisive experimental confirmation, and has had deep downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group observed edge transport in HgTe quantum wells; Hasan's group established the 3D topological insulator through ARPES. Three names from the supplied list give a balanced theory/experiment configuration, but this requires leaving out Eugene Mele, whose joint role with Kane is a real attribution difficulty; Bernevig/Zhang's HgTe prediction is not on the list at all.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation. Highly mature, though the prize committee has to resolve overlap with the other topological-insulator candidate and with the 2016 recognition of topological phases.
uncertainties: Omission of Mele and of the HgTe theory proposers.
Overlap with the other topological-insulator and quantum-anomalous-Hall candidates on the same theme.
2016 prize already covered topological phases of matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies: the discovery of a diffuse astrophysical flux in 2013 and later associations with a blazar and the Galactic plane. It is a discovery with clear experimental identity, impressive instrument invention and lasting astrophysical significance.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the principal intellectual driver of the concept; Karle and Yoshida are key collaboration leaders. IceCube is a large collaboration (and AMANDA preceded it), so crediting three individuals is inherently arbitrary and I regard allocation as a real issue under the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established; source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma individually and still developing. Recognition is plausible but arguably slightly early for a source-level result.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit cannot be cleanly assigned to three individuals.
Source associations are not yet at discovery significance for all claims.
Whether the 2002 prize for cosmic neutrinos reduces perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state quantum platform for sensing, imaging and quantum information. As a microscopy-minded member I value the nanoscale magnetometry, but the underlying discovery is the single-spin optical addressing.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-NV optically detected magnetic resonance and coherent control; Lukin contributed major proposals and demonstrations of quantum registers and sensing. The three supplied names are reasonable, though Gruber/Wrachtrup 1997 and the broader community (Awschalom, Hanson) are not in the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups and widely applied, with commercial and biological uses. The field is mature, though the sensing applications are still evolving.
uncertainties: Awschalom and Hanson groups' role is not represented.
Whether the prize should centre on the single-spin discovery or on applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions underlies hard-drive read heads and MRAM, and is a case where interface quality and spin-dependent tunnelling were decisive. The importance is high, with the fundamental physics resting on atomic-scale interface control.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's work on MgO and on sputtered tunnel barriers, together with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, was needed for giant effect sizes. The supplied triple is defensible but omits the MgO crystalline-barrier discoverers, and the 2007 prize on giant magnetoresistance may shade the novelty.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of technological deployment and independent reproduction.
uncertainties: Credit for coherent MgO tunnelling is split among people not on the list.
Closeness to the 2007 GMR prize may count against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are a decisive materials invention, the strongest permanent magnets, and underpin wind turbines, electric vehicles and drives. It meets the 'discovery or invention' criterion in a way that is concrete and widely beneficial, although the associated physics is largely materials engineering of a known class of compounds.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered route, Sumitomo) and Croat (melt-spun, General Motors) announced the compound essentially simultaneously in 1983-84; two names is a clean configuration, though priority claims in Japan and the United States were contested.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use make the lasting impact unquestionable, and recognition is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as physics rather than materials science or chemistry.
Priority dispute between the two groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission became the central momentum-resolved probe of quantum materials, notably in the cuprates, giving direct access to band structure, gaps and many-body self-energies. It is an instrumental and methodological advance of broad lasting impact, close to my own domain of spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano's group and Shen's group produced the landmark cuprate Fermi-surface and gap measurements; Johnson contributed early methods. A method-based prize is harder to attribute, since the technique grew out of many decades of photoemission work (Siegbahn, Plummer, Himpsel and others are not on the list).
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently used worldwide. Recognition is not premature, but the committee would need a clearly delimited discovery rather than a technique in general.
uncertainties: Technique prize versus discovery prize.
Credit overlap with earlier photoemission pioneers and with the Siegbahn 1981 prize.
Selection of Shen and Campuzano over Johnson is a judgement.
